title: JSON vs Natural Prompts for Veo 3 Video

sections.heading: Everyday Analogy - Recipe Note vs Recipe Form
sections.body:
Think of asking a friend to cook.

A natural prompt is like a note: "make a cool red dress video, dark and fancy." Your friend guesses the details.

A JSON prompt is like a filled form with boxes: lighting: red, style: cinematic, cut: invisible. JSON means JavaScript Object Notation, a way to write labeled boxes for a computer. Veo 3 is Google's AI that makes video from text.

Both can make the same red fashion video, but the form gives tighter control.

sections.heading: Why it exists
sections.body:
Natural language is fast but vague. Words like "cinematic" or "seamless" can mean many things.

JSON prompting exists to be precise. You set separate controls for lighting, style, and cuts. An invisible cut is an edit hidden to look like one continuous shot.

In your save, both prompts made the same dark red surreal concept, but JSON let the creator steer the exact look and transition.

sections.heading: What can go wrong
sections.body:
More control means more ways to fail.

- Too many or wrong labels can confuse Veo 3 and make a stiff or broken video.
- Small typos in JSON, like a missing bracket, can make the whole prompt fail.
- Over-specifying can kill creativity, giving a perfect but boring result.

steps.narration: Start with your idea for the video.
Natural prompt sends it as one vague sentence.
JSON prompt splits it into labeled boxes for lighting and cuts.
Veo 3 reads the prompt and builds the video.
You get the seamless transition, more precise with JSON.

quiz.q: What is JSON prompting in Veo 3?
options: A way to write prompts as labeled boxes for precise control
A way to make videos without any prompt
A filter that only changes music
quiz.why: Your save shows JSON prompting uses structured labels to control cinematic style, lighting, and cuts more precisely than natural language.

quiz.q: Why use JSON instead of just natural language?
options: JSON lets you control each part like lighting and cuts separately
JSON is always faster to type
quiz.why: Natural prompts are vague, JSON exists to give separate, precise controls for the same concept.

quiz.q: What breaks or goes wrong if you make your JSON prompt 100x more detailed?
options: Veo 3 will always make it perfect
Small typos or conflicting labels can make the video fail or look stiff
The video will automatically become shorter
quiz.why: Over-specifying with too many boxes increases typos and conflicts, which can confuse the model and break the seamless result.
